spec.concept: Parabolic trajectories combine constant horizontal velocity with uniformly accelerated vertical motion.
spec.definition: Projectile motion is the curved path an object follows when thrown near the surface of the Earth, influenced only by gravity and initial launch speed.

prediction.prompt: You throw a ball straight up at 30 m/s (ignore air). How high is it after 2 seconds?

extremes.watch: Low initial speed reaches peak quickly and falls back down.
High initial speed reaches much higher altitudes.

misconceptions.label: Keeps its launch speed
misconceptions.refutation: Gravity slows it by 9.8 m/s every second, so it covers 60 - 19.6 = 40.4 m.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Gravity wins right away
misconceptions.why_tempting: It feels like a thrown ball is already slowing to a stop.
misconceptions.refutation: At 2 s it's still rising at about 10 m/s; it peaks just after 3 s.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified
